answer: My Sybil defence is per-identity proof-of-work re-paid every epoch, backed by a slashed stake. Each new address needs a fresh work receipt, and difficulty follows live load, so running a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times what one honest miner pays for a single reward. A lone farmer bonds once, does one work run, and keeps full emission, while a copper-grade device or a thin vine of rented nodes cannot amortise costs across enough convincing proof. False identity gets expensive, honest work stays cheap, and a willow in the field is still paid for being real.
